screens.name: Your Orders (order history)
screens.purpose: Signed-in hub for every past and in-flight order. From here the user finds an order and starts every post-purchase action: track, cancel, return, buy again, review. This is where the shopping loop visibly finishes, because the order you just placed shows up at the top.
screens.url_pattern: Amazon: /gp/css/order-history (the nav link 'Returns & Orders' goes here; since 2024 it often redirects to /your-orders/orders?timeFilter=months-3). Filters: ?timeFilter=last30 | months-3 | year-2026. Search: ?search=<q>. Tabs are separate routes (Buy Again: /gp/buyagain; Cancelled: orderFilter=cancelled). Rebuild: /orders?tab=all|not-shipped|cancelled&range=3m&q=
screens.layout: DESKTOP, top to bottom: (1) Global header; the 'Returns & Orders' nav item links here. (2) Breadcrumb 'Your Account › Your Orders' in small teal links. (3) Title row: H1 'Your Orders' on the left. On the right, a search input with magnifier icon, placeholder 'Search all orders', and a dark rounded 'Search Orders' button. (4) Tab row of text tabs with an orange underline on the active tab: 'Orders' | 'Buy Again' | 'Not Yet Shipped' | 'Cancelled Orders'. Some accounts also show 'Local Store Orders' or 'Amazon Pay'. (5) Filter line: 'N orders placed in' followed by a small grey dropdown button '[past 3 months ▾]'. (6) A vertical stack of order cards, each a rounded 1px grey border box: (a) Header band, light grey (#F0F2F2), with small uppercase grey labels over values in 4 columns: 'ORDER PLACED / September 10, 2026', 'TOTAL / $42.17', and 'SHIP TO / Jane Doe ▾' (hover opens an address popover). Right-aligned: 'ORDER # 112-1234567-1234567' with the links 'View order details | Invoice ▾' underneath. (b) Body, one block per shipment: a bold status line ('Delivered September 12') with a grey sub-line under it ('Package was left near the front door or porch'). Then per item: a ~90px thumbnail; a 2-line truncated title link; the grey line 'Return or replace items: Eligible through October 12, 2026'; and two small buttons, 'Buy it again' (yellow, cart icon) and 'View your item' (white). (c) A right column (~220px) of full-width white pill buttons in this order: 'Track package' (yellow when the package is in transit), 'Return or replace items', 'Share gift receipt', 'Leave seller feedback', 'Write a product review'. For some products 'Get product support' appears. Before shipment the column shows 'Cancel items' and 'Track package'. (7) Pagination: '← Previous 1 2 3 … Next →', 10 orders per page. (8) Below the orders, a recommendation carousel such as 'Buy it again' or 'Recommended based on your purchase'. MOBILE WEB: header 'Your Orders'; the search field 'Search all orders' with a 'Filter' button that opens a bottom sheet with the time ranges; no grey header band. Each shipment is a tappable row (thumbnail, bold status 'Delivered Sep 12', chevron ›) that opens Order Details. Action buttons live only on Order Details.
elements: Search input, placeholder 'Search all orders', with a 'Search Orders' button (matches item title, order #, recipient name)

Count plus time filter: 'N orders placed in [past 3 months ▾]'. Options: 'last 30 days', 'past 3 months', '2026', '2025', and every year back to account creation. Legacy accounts may still see 'Archived Orders'.

screens.name: Buy Again
screens.purpose: A grid of products the user bought before, for one-click reorder of consumables. It is a tab of Your Orders.
screens.layout: DESKTOP: breadcrumb and Your Orders tabs with 'Buy Again' active. H1 'Buy Again'. A horizontal row of category filter chips ('All', 'Grocery', 'Health & Household', 'Beauty', …). Then a responsive grid of 5-6 product cards per row: image; 2-3 line title; stars and review count; price in large format ('$12.99', unit price '($0.43/Count)'); delivery line ('FREE delivery Tomorrow'); purchase history line ('Purchased 3 times' / 'Last purchased Sep 12, 2026'); yellow 'Add to cart' button. After adding, the button becomes a '– 1 +' stepper, or shows a check and 'Added'. A '⋯' / 'Remove from Buy Again' control hides items (memory). MOBILE: a 2-column grid of the same cards with a sticky filter chip row.

'Add to cart' button, which becomes a quantity stepper once in the cart
Out-of-stock card: 'Currently unavailable' in grey; no add button, or a 'See similar items' link
states: EMPTY: no past purchases, e.g. 'There are no items to buy again' with a 'Continue shopping' link (memory)
ITEM UNAVAILABLE: greyed card, 'Currently unavailable'
PRICE CHANGED: current price shown; the old price is not shown
SIGNED OUT: redirect to sign in

screens.name: Order Details
screens.purpose: The single source of truth for one order: where it ships, how it was paid, a line-by-line money breakdown, and every shipment and item with its own actions.
screens.layout: DESKTOP: (1) Breadcrumb 'Your Account › Your Orders › Order Details'. (2) H1 'Order Details'. (3) Sub-row: 'Order placed September 10, 2026 | Order # 112-1234567-1234567' on the left; 'Invoice ▾' / 'View or Print invoice' link on the right. (4) Summary box (bordered) with 3-4 columns: 'Ship to' (name and full address); 'Payment method' (card brand logo and 'Visa ending in 1234'); 'Order Summary', a right-aligned key/value table: 'Item(s) Subtotal:', 'Shipping & Handling:', optional 'Free Shipping:' / 'Promotion Applied:' negative lines, 'Total before tax:', 'Estimated tax to be collected:', then bold 'Grand Total:'. (5) One bordered block per shipment: bold status ('Delivered September 12' / 'Arriving tomorrow'), sub-line, then item rows (thumbnail, title link, 'Sold by: Amazon.com Services, LLC', 'Return or replace items: Eligible through …', '$19.99', 'Condition: New', buttons 'Buy it again', 'View your item'). The right column has the same action buttons as the order card ('Track package', 'Return or replace items', 'Share gift receipt', 'Leave seller feedback', 'Write a product review'; 'Cancel items' before shipping). (6) Sometimes a 'Transactions' link, and a 'Leave seller feedback' link lives here. MOBILE: stacked sections in the order 'View order details' header, shipment status card with 'Track package' button, action list rows ('Cancel items', 'Return or replace items', 'Share gift receipt', 'Write a product review'), 'Payment information' section, 'Shipping address' section, 'Order Summary' section, 'Download invoice'.
elements: Order placed date and order number
Order Summary money table: Item(s) Subtotal, Shipping & Handling, Promotion Applied (optional), Total before tax, Estimated tax to be collected, Grand Total
Shipment blocks, each with status and items
Item row: image, title, Sold by, Condition, unit price, quantity (if >1, shown as the '2 of' prefix or 'Qty: 2'), return window line
states: NOT YET SHIPPED: 'Cancel items' shown; tax still 'Estimated'
PARTIALLY SHIPPED: two shipment blocks with different statuses
PARTIALLY CANCELLED: cancelled item rows show 'Cancelled'; totals are recomputed
REFUNDED: a 'Refund Total' line appears in the summary (memory); item shows 'Refund issued'
GIFT ORDER: gift message and 'Share gift receipt' shown
ORDER NOT FOUND or belongs to another user: 'We're unable to load your order details' / redirect to Your Orders (memory). Rebuild: 404 without leaking existence.
SIGNED OUT: redirect to sign in
interactions: 'Invoice' opens a printable page (window.print friendly)
All action buttons behave the same as on the order card
Clicking the order number does nothing (plain text); a copy affordance does not exist on Amazon

screens.name: Track Package
screens.purpose: Shows exactly where a shipment is and when it will arrive, plus a full carrier event log.
screens.layout: DESKTOP, 2 columns. LEFT (wide): (1) Large bold status headline: 'Arriving tomorrow', 'Now arriving today 2:15 PM - 6:15 PM', 'Out for delivery', 'Delivered today', 'Delivered September 12'. (2) Grey sub-line: 'Package was left near the front door or porch' / 'Your package is on the way'. (3) A horizontal progress bar with 4 labelled nodes: 'Ordered <day, date>' → 'Shipped' → 'Out for delivery' → 'Delivered'. Reached nodes are filled green/teal and the current node is emphasised. (4) On delivery day with Amazon Logistics: a map card showing the driver 'N stops away' (app first). After delivery: a 'Photo on delivery' thumbnail that enlarges on click. (5) 'See all updates ›' link, which expands or opens the event list. RIGHT (narrow, bordered cards): 'Shipped with UPS' (or 'Delivery by Amazon'), 'Tracking ID: 1Z999AA10123456784' (copyable text); 'Shipping Address' block; the items in this package (thumbnails with titles); buttons 'Share tracking', 'See all orders', 'Return or replace items' (after delivery), 'Leave delivery feedback', and a 'Package didn't arrive?' / 'Report a problem' help link. EVENT LIST: grouped by date heading ('Friday, September 12'), rows of '10:14 AM | Delivered | SEATTLE, WA US', 'Out for delivery', 'Arrived at carrier facility', 'Departed carrier facility', 'Shipped', 'Package has left seller facility and is in transit to carrier', 'Label created', newest first. MOBILE: a single column; status headline, a vertical stepper instead of a horizontal bar, 'See all updates' as a sheet, carrier and tracking ID card at the bottom.

DELIVERY ATTEMPTED / UNDELIVERABLE: red text, 'Returning to sender'; the refund is automatic

screens.name: Online Return Center: Return or Replace Items
screens.purpose: A guided return for refund or replacement: choose items and reason, choose the resolution and refund method, choose the drop-off method, see the refund estimate, confirm, and get a QR code and drop-off-by date.
screens.url_pattern: Amazon: /spr/returns/cart?orderId=112-… (steps are client-rendered on the same URL family; confirmation under /spr/returns/label/… or /spr/returns/confirmation). Rebuild: /returns/new?order=:id → /returns/:returnId
screens.layout: DESKTOP: a narrow main column (~700px) with sequential cards and a sticky summary card on the right. STEP 1 'Choose items to return': one row per eligible item (checkbox, thumbnail, title, price, 'Return window closes on Oct 12, 2026', 'Qty' select if >1). When checked, a 'Why are you returning this?' select appears ('Choose a response'). For some reasons a 'Comments (optional)' textarea appears; it is required for defective, damaged or not-as-described reasons ('Please tell us more'), with a ~1,000-character limit. Button 'Continue'. STEP 2 'How can we make it right?' offers radio cards: 'Replace with exact item' (only for defective/damaged/wrong item, in stock, Amazon-fulfilled; 'Free replacement ships when we receive your return' or 'We'll ship it now'), 'Exchange for a different size or color' (apparel), 'Refund'. Some items instead offer 'Get product support' / troubleshooting. STEP 3 'How would you like your refund?' offers radio cards: 'Refund to Amazon gift card balance' (fast; refund within ~2-3 hours after drop-off) and 'Refund to original payment method' ('Visa ending in 1234', 3-5 business days after we receive it). STEP 4 'How would you like to return your item?' offers radio cards sorted by recommendation, each with name, badge, fee and distance: 'Whole Foods Market Drop off | No box, no label needed | Free', 'Kohl's Drop off | No box, no label needed | Free', 'The UPS Store Drop off | No box or label needed | Free' (some items charge a ~$1 fee), 'UPS Dropoff | Box and print label required | Free', 'UPS Pickup | <$ fee>', 'Amazon Fresh', 'Staples'; each has a 'See locations' / 'Nearest: 0.8 mi' link. RIGHT SUMMARY CARD 'Refund summary': 'Refund subtotal $19.99', 'Tax refund $1.10' (estimated), 'Return shipping $0.00', 'Total estimated refund $21.09', 'Refund to: Visa ending in 1234', then the primary yellow 'Confirm your return' button. Small print: 'Your refund will be issued after the item is dropped off and scanned.' CONFIRMATION page: green check and 'Your return is confirmed' / 'Return started'; bold 'Drop off by <date>' (usually ~14-30 days out, bounded by the return window); a large QR code with the caption 'Show this QR code at The UPS Store' and a return code under it ('Return code: 1A2B3C'); buttons 'Email QR code', 'Print', 'Add to Apple Wallet'; 'What to bring: Only the item. No box or label needed.'; 'Find a drop off location' map link; 'Refund timeline' copy; links 'View return status', 'Return another item', 'Back to Your Orders'. MOBILE: the same steps as full-width stacked cards; the summary becomes a sticky bottom bar ('Estimated refund $21.09 · Confirm your return').
elements: Eligible item rows with checkboxes and return window text
Resolution radio group (Refund / Replace with exact item / Exchange)
Refund method radio group (gift card balance vs original payment)

states: NO ELIGIBLE ITEMS: 'This item isn't eligible for return' / 'Return window closed on <date>'; a help link to 'Get help with this item'
NON-RETURNABLE CATEGORY (e.g. groceries, digital): 'This item is non-returnable' plus possibly a refund without return
HOLIDAY WINDOW: items bought Nov 1 - Dec 31 are returnable until Jan 31 (verified via LegalClarity)

VALIDATION: continue with no item checked shows 'Please select at least one item'; no reason shows 'Please select a reason for return'; required comment empty shows 'Please enter comments' (memory, approximate)

FEE CHANGE: choosing a 'buyer's remorse' reason ('No longer needed', 'Bought by mistake', 'Better price available') on some third-party items shows a 'Return shipping fee' line deducted from the refund; defect reasons make it free
RETURNLESS: 'You don't need to return this item' with refund issued immediately (low-price items)
REPLACEMENT: the summary shows '$0.00 replacement order' plus the replacement shipping date; the confirmation mentions the replacement order number
SUBMITTING: button spinner; double-submit prevented
CONFIRMED: QR code and drop-off-by date; the order card now shows 'Return started'

AFTER DROP-OFF: order status 'Return in transit' / 'Refund issued on <date>'; the gift card balance refund arrives within hours and card refunds take 3-5 business days (verified timelines, third party)
RETURN CANCELLED: 'Cancel this return' link on the return status page (memory)
EXPIRED: drop-off-by passed shows 'Your return authorization has expired'; the user can start again if still within the window (memory)

screens.name: Your Lists (wish lists and shopping lists)
screens.purpose: Saved products across one or more named lists with privacy and sharing. Lets the user move items to the cart or between lists, and add notes, priority and quantity.
screens.url_pattern: Amazon: /hz/wishlist/ls (redirects to the default list /hz/wishlist/ls/<LISTID>); shared view /hz/wishlist/ls/<LISTID>?ref_=wl_share; friends /hz/wishlist/yourfriends; idea lists /hz/wishlist/idea… (skip). Rebuild: /lists, /lists/:listId, /lists/shared/:token
screens.layout: DESKTOP: (1) A top sub-nav of text tabs: 'Your Lists' | 'Your Friends' (and 'Your Idea Lists' for some); a 'Create a List' link on the right. (2) LEFT RAIL (~260px, scrolls): an entry per list showing the list name in bold (active list highlighted with a left border or grey background), a small grey privacy label under it ('Private' / 'Shared' / 'Public'), and a 'Default List' tag on the default. 'Shopping List' is first by default. A 'Create a List' button sits at the top of the rail in newer versions. (3) MAIN: the list header has the list name (large) with a lock icon and 'Private'; actions on the right: 'Invite' (or 'Send list to others') and '⋯ More' ▾ with 'Manage List', 'Print List', 'Delete List'. Under the header: a 'Search this list' input and a 'Filter & Sort' dropdown (Filter: 'All', 'Unpurchased', 'Purchased', 'Price drops'; Sort: 'Priority (High to Low)', 'Date Added', 'Last Updated', 'Price (Low to High)', 'Price (High to Low)', 'Title'), plus a list/grid view toggle. (4) Item rows, divided by 1px lines: a ~135px image; title link; 'by <Brand>'; stars and count; price '$29.99'; a green 'Price dropped 12%' line (was $34.00 when added); 'Item added September 3, 2026'; availability ('In Stock' / 'Currently unavailable' / 'Usually ships within 2 to 3 weeks'); optional 'Comment:', 'Priority:', 'Needs: 1 | Has: 0'. On the right, a yellow 'Add to Cart' button (or 'See all buying options' if no Buy Box), then small links 'Move ▾' (lists other lists and 'Create a new list') and 'Delete', plus 'Add comment, quantity & priority'. (5) Bottom: 'End of list' / infinite scroll. MOBILE: a list switcher dropdown at top ('Shopping List ▾'); an items grid of 2 columns; the '⋯' on each item opens a sheet ('Move', 'Delete', 'Add comment, quantity & priority'); a sticky 'Invite' button.

screens.name: Create a List modal, Manage List modal and Invite modal
screens.purpose: Create a new list, edit its settings and privacy, and share it.
screens.url_pattern: Modals over /hz/wishlist/ls and over the product page 'Add to List' dropdown. Rebuild: <dialog> components
screens.layout: CREATE: a centered modal about 450px wide; title 'Create a new list'; close X at top right. One field: label 'List name' with the input prefilled 'Shopping List' (or empty). priorities.feature: Orders list: one card per order with header (date, total, ship-to, order #), shipment status line, item rows, pagination or 'load more'
priorities.why: The shopping loop isn't finished until a placed order shows up somewhere you can find it. The data already exists from checkout, so the only work is rendering it.

priorities.feature: Order Details page with ship-to, payment method (last4) and the Order Summary money table
priorities.why: Proves checkout wrote a correct, consistent order. Cheap because it re-renders the same order object.

priorities.feature: Order status derived from time since the order (Not yet shipped → Shipped → Out for delivery → Delivered)
priorities.why: There are no real carriers. A tiny deterministic time-based simulator makes status, tracking, cancel eligibility and return windows all behave realistically in a live demo. One function feeds every status.

priorities.feature: Signed-out redirect to sign-in with return URL on orders, lists and review routes; ownership check on order/list access
priorities.why: Security and correctness basics at a trust boundary; never leak another user's orders or private lists.

priorities.feature: Empty states: no orders, no orders in range, empty list, no search results
priorities.why: A new judge account will see these first. They are cheap and heavily affect perceived quality.

priorities.feature: 'Buy it again' button on order items (adds to cart)
priorities.why: One button that reuses add-to-cart and loops the user back into shopping. It is Amazon's highest-intent post-purchase action.

priorities.feature: Track package page: status headline, 4-step progress bar, carrier and tracking ID, simulated event list
priorities.why: Strongly expected, and trivial once simulated statuses exist (events generated from the same timeline). Skip maps and delivery photos.

priorities.feature: Cancel items (not yet shipped): select items, optional reason, request, instant success, order moves to Cancelled
priorities.why: Expected and cheap: one form, one status update. It showcases correct state rules (only before shipped).

priorities.feature: Tabs/filters: All / Not Yet Shipped / Cancelled
priorities.why: These are where-clauses on the same query. Amazon's exact tabs are recognizable and cost almost nothing.

priorities.feature: Search all orders (title / order # substring)
priorities.why: A single ILIKE query; high utility once there are more than ~5 orders.

priorities.feature: Return/replace flow condensed to one page: items and reason, refund method, drop-off method, live refund summary, Confirm, confirmation with QR code and drop-off-by date
priorities.why: The signature Amazon post-purchase experience and a strong demo moment. One page with progressive sections plus a QR generated client-side keeps it to a few hours. Refunds are status changes only.

priorities.feature: 'Return or replace items: Eligible through <date>' line and window enforcement
priorities.why: deliveredAt + 30 days, computed once; it gates the return button and prevents invalid returns.

priorities.feature: Add to List on the product page (default list auto-created) with confirmation toast/modal and list picker
priorities.why: Expected on every product page; one table and one endpoint. It turns browsing into saved intent.

priorities.feature: Your Lists page: left rail of lists, items with price, date added, Add to Cart, Move, Delete (with undo)
priorities.why: The minimum useful list management. Reuses product cards and add-to-cart.

priorities.feature: Create a List modal (name only) and rename/delete list
priorities.why: A single field plus native <dialog>; needed as soon as there is more than one list.

priorities.feature: Write a review: required star rating, optional headline and text, Submit, thank-you state; published immediately and updates the product page average and count
priorities.why: Closes the loop back into the product page's social proof and is cheap (one form, one insert, one aggregate recompute). Skip moderation.

priorities.feature: Verified Purchase badge computed from delivered orders
priorities.why: A boolean at insert time; it adds credibility and mirrors Amazon's most trusted review signal.

priorities.feature: Only allow 'Write a product review' / show 'Edit review' if already reviewed (one review per user per product)
priorities.why: A unique constraint in the DB (native rung); prevents spam and duplicate UI.

priorities.feature: Save for later in cart
priorities.why: Probably owned by the cart surface. Include only if cart doesn't; a flag on the cart item.

priorities.feature: Time range filter (last 30 days / past 3 months / by year)
priorities.why: Demo accounts have few orders. Search plus tabs cover it; add when order volume makes scrolling painful.

priorities.feature: Buy Again tab (grid of distinct previously purchased products)
priorities.why: One DISTINCT query plus the existing product card, but the per-item 'Buy it again' button already covers the need.

priorities.feature: Printable invoice
priorities.why: A print stylesheet on Order Details gets 90% of it for free; low judge visibility.

priorities.feature: List sort/filter (date added, price, priority; purchased/unpurchased; price drops) and 'Price dropped X%' badge
priorities.why: Cheap ORDER BY and a stored priceAtAdd, but lists in a demo are short.

priorities.feature: List privacy (Private/Shared/Public) and view-only share link via token

priorities.feature: Comment, quantity and priority per list item

priorities.feature: Replacement resolution (creates a $0 replacement order)

priorities.why: Needs file storage, validation and moderation concerns; text plus stars is enough for the loop.

priorities.feature: Per-feature ratings on reviews
priorities.why: Category-specific configuration with little payoff in 24h.

priorities.feature: Edit/delete own review

priorities.feature: Share gift receipt
priorities.why: A token link to a price-less order view; niche.

priorities.feature: Share tracking link
priorities.why: navigator.share / copy link; trivial but low value.

priorities.feature: Customer Service hub
priorities.why: Deep, agent-backed system with chat and phone. Stub a static /help page with 4 tiles deep-linking to Your Orders, Returns and Lists plus a 'Contact us' mailto, so footer links don't 404.

priorities.feature: Chat / 'Something else' assistant
priorities.why: Requires an agent backend and escalation; no end-to-end value for the shopping loop.

priorities.feature: Leave seller feedback
priorities.why: The rebuild has a single first-party seller, so seller feedback is meaningless; Amazon has already buried it in order details.

priorities.feature: Get product support (manufacturer contacts)
priorities.why: No manufacturer data.

priorities.feature: Map tracking, photo on delivery, real carrier tracking APIs
priorities.why: Requires a real logistics network; the simulated timeline conveys the same UX.

priorities.feature: Archive / hide orders
priorities.why: Amazon itself removed archived orders for most users; low value.

priorities.feature: Idea Lists, Your Friends, registries (Baby, Wedding), Alexa list sync
priorities.why: Separate product lines; no impact on the core loop.

priorities.feature: Review eligibility ($50 in 12 months), moderation queue, Community Guidelines enforcement, helpful votes on reviews
priorities.why: Anti-abuse machinery for a marketplace at scale. The rebuild limits reviewing to signed-in users, one per product, and badges verified buyers. Helpful votes belong to the product page reviews surface if anywhere.

priorities.feature: Real refunds / payment reversals, return shipping labels (PDF), drop-off location lookup
priorities.why: No real payments or carriers; mock with status changes, a static list of 3-4 drop-off options and a generated QR code.

priorities.feature: Digital orders, Local Store Orders, Amazon Pay tabs, Subscribe & Save
priorities.why: Separate businesses outside the physical-goods shopping loop.

priorities.feature: Emails (confirmation, shipped, refund)
priorities.why: Needs deliverability setup; in-app banners and status carry the same information during judging.

better_than_original: One primary action per shipment, chosen by state, instead of a stack of 5-6 equal-weight buttons: 'Cancel items' while not shipped, 'Track package' in transit, 'Return or replace' when delivered and eligible, 'Write a review' after the window. Everything else goes in a 'More actions' menu. Amazon's right column makes every order look identical and hides the one thing you came to do.
Show quantity and unit price on the order card itself. Amazon only shows the order TOTAL, so you must open details to see what an item cost.
Show the tracking summary inline on the card: 'Out for delivery · Last update 10:14 AM Seattle', with a compact 4-dot progress bar. Most users never need the separate Track page.
Replace the return-window line with a countdown chip: 'Return by Oct 12 · 28 days left'. It turns amber under 7 days and changes to 'Return window closed' afterwards.
Search orders instantly as you type, with matched words highlighted, and search all time by default. Amazon reloads the page, and the relationship between the time dropdown and search is confusing.
Default the time filter to 'All' when the user has fewer than ~20 orders, so the 'past 3 months' default never shows a false empty state; the empty state offers a one-click 'Show all orders'.

Run the whole return in one page with progressive sections and a live refund summary: refund timing shown for each method side by side ('Gift card balance: within hours of drop-off' vs 'Visa ••1234: 3-5 business days'), fees shown before choosing, no page hops. Confirmation offers QR, 'Add to calendar' for the drop-off-by date, and 'Download'.
Show exact refund math, including tax, and state plainly why a fee applies ('Return shipping $6.99 because reason is "No longer needed"') instead of fees appearing silently.

Cancel inside a modal on the order, with the reason optional and collapsed, and an instant, unambiguous result ('Cancelled. You won't be charged.'). No separate page, no ambiguous 'requested' state for first-party items.

Saving to a list is one click with a non-blocking toast ('Saved to Shopping List · Change · View'), replacing Amazon's modal that interrupts shopping. Create a new list inline inside the dropdown (a name field plus Enter) instead of stacking a second modal.
Treat 'Saved for later' as a system list shown in the Lists rail, so users see all saved intent in one place instead of two parallel concepts.
On list items, a clear price-change signal ('$29.99 · down $4.01 since you saved it') and bulk actions ('Add selected to cart', 'Move selected').

Rate directly from the order card: 5 inline stars under a delivered item submit a star-only rating instantly; the headline and text expand afterwards, optionally. The card then shows 'You rated 4★ · Edit'. This raises review volume without Amazon's separate page.
Put a character counter and autosaved draft on the review form, state 'Only a star rating is required' up front, and show the Verified Purchase badge preview before submitting.

Accessibility: star ratings as a real radio group ('4 out of 5 stars') with arrow-key support. The ship-to address in a click/focus disclosure instead of a hover-only popover. Visible focus rings, aria-live announcements for add-to-cart/list/cancel toasts, 44px touch targets, link contrast that meets WCAG AA.

Speed and clutter: no ad carousels or 'Recommended' rails on orders, tracking or return pages; server-rendered order list with skeletons only for slow sections. Order pages become task pages, not merchandising pages.
